parts.note: top as an adjective means best, as in the top student
a mount is a horse to ride, and to mount is to ride it; ride serves as noun or verb

explanation.surface: A riddle-like question: is straddling simply the finest way to get on a horse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'top mount?' reads like a phrase about climbing on, but it splits into two synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to sit or stand with a leg on each side of it, exactly what straddling means.

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
PE is physical education, i.e. school exercise

explanation.surface: A vagrant got shoved around on the day set aside for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bumped is to be knocked or pushed into, which is what jostled means.

clue.text: Sailor is sorry after fall from grace

indicators.note: after places the word for sorry behind the word for wrongdoing

parts.note: a sin is a moral failing, a fall from grace
to feel bad is to feel sorry

explanation.surface: A seafarer feels remorse after a moral lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. Sinbad is the legendary sailor of the Arabian Nights tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the famous seafarer of the Arabian Nights, so he is an example of a sailor.

indicators.note: in a down clue upstanding means the letters read from the bottom up, so backwards
practically means almost, so the final letter of the word for formal is dropped

parts.note: stiff manners are formal and starchy
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An upright, rather stiff monarch brings things up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' trims STIFF to STIF; add ER and 'Upstanding' reads STIFER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit something is to re-equip it with new fittings, bringing it up to date.

parts.note: the family jewels are heirlooms; to take away an heir's claim to them is to cut them out of a will

explanation.surface: A cheeky hint at castration, family jewels being slang for the testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family jewels' suggests the slang meaning; read literally they are heirlooms that an heir would inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to prevent an heir from receiving their inheritance, such as the family heirlooms.

clue.text: Confusion of curious cat losing tail

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or curious

indicators.note: losing its tail tells us to cut the final letter off the word for cat

parts.note: puss is an informal word for a cat

explanation.surface: An odd cat that has lost its tail is understandably in a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' removes the final S. 'Curious' here means strange, a dated British sense of rum, not inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, a scene of confusion.

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter; both words lose theirs

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
the remaining ones are the other ones

explanation.surface: A family member left standing with no trousers on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without bottoms' strips the last letter from each word: UNCLE loses E, OTHER loses R. 'bottoms' also hints at trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare is to uncover; to unclothe is to strip off clothes, uncovering the body.

indicators.note: saving in the sense of keeping safe inside means one word holds the other

parts.note: a march is a procession or parade
lives as in exists, the verb is

explanation.surface: A protest march that rescues people is seen as heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescuing but means holding: PARADE holds IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a synonym for Heaven, the abode of the blessed.

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word sea-god's

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: Neptune's weapon is his chief possession, crashing like the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: A trident is the three-pronged spear carried by the sea-god Neptune or Poseidon, so the surface hangs together.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, as a thundering voice is.

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, ... means plain to see, open and obvious
as a verb, to ... is to show or present something, as a symptom does

explanation.surface: Two words that look like an instruction to unwrap a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests unwrapping a present; instead each word is a separate sense of the answer, one adjective and one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest describes something openly evident, and also means to display or exhibit, matching both words.

clue.text: Someone counting overs, recording every run initially

definitions.text: Someone counting overs, recording every run initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the six preceding words in turn

explanation.surface: A description of the official at a cricket match who logs each over and every run scored.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the first letters of its six words spell the answer. In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, and runs are the points scored.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the scorer is the official who keeps count of overs bowled and records every run made.

parts.note: an ex is a former partner or sweetheart
an actor playing a role is acting

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is playing hard to get, with the dots running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing hard' looks like the phrase 'playing hard to get', but 'playing' belongs with the wordplay and 'hard' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task is hard and demanding, requiring great effort or care.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are to be heard, not read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to see someone is to date them, so dated gives saw; accomplished a task means did it

explanation.surface: Continuing the former sweetheart story: the ex apparently dated and achieved something seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells us SAW DID, said in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the answer. To 'see' someone means to date them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid describes something morally low or squalid, the same idea as degenerate used as an adjective.

clue.text: Consider composer almost penning 'Time after Time'

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals
almost means the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer, of the ballet Coppélia

indicators.note: after puts the first time abbreviation behind the second

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Thinking about a musician who nearly wrote a song called Time After Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the composer's last letter, and 'penning' encloses the two times, the second Time coming first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to think carefully about something, i.e. consider it.

parts.note: hide here is animal skin, i.e. leather, and pants are trousers: trousers made of leather, not a command to conceal underwear

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction to conceal your underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is a noun meaning leather; 'pants' is the noun for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are traditional Alpine leather shorts or breeches, literally trousers of hide.

clue.text: What's often said in church following worshipper

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken at a church wedding
later means following on afterwards

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is defined by the words they recite and come after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' is the reply couples give in the wedding vows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is someone who worships idols, so a kind of worshipper.

clue.text: Trigger's entrance with rogues Del and Rodney?

indicators.note: entrance means the start, so the first letter of Trigger's

parts.note: rotters are scoundrels or rogues

explanation.surface: A scene from the sitcom where Trigger walks in on the Trotter brothers' dodgy dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy and Rodney Trotter are the wheeler-dealing brothers of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; Trigger is their dim friend in the same show.
explanation.definitionFit: Del and Rodney share the surname Trotter, so together they are the Trotters, defined by example.

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means the judging word sits beneath the material

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric or material
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A judge backs a piece of evidence in a torture case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' in a down clue puts RATE underneath LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear flesh, and figuratively to cause great pain or distress, close to torture.

clue.text: Taken from under mat? It isn't rash

indicators.note: taken from says the answer is extracted from the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone retrieving something from under a doormat insists it is not a reckless move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective meaning reckless, but it is the noun for a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatitis is inflammation of the skin, which shows itself as a rash.

indicators.note: around says the word for firm surrounds the central letter

parts.note: stuck means fixed firm, unable to move

indicators.note: mid asks for the middle letter of the nine-letter word afternoon

explanation.surface: A company knocked off work halfway through the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but means fixed. 'mid' takes R, the fifth of afternoon's nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who struck went on strike, stopping work in protest; the question mark marks this second sense.

indicators.note: to wear means the church abbreviation goes around the other word like a garment

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to put on their Sunday best for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' makes the church abbreviation the garment, surrounding the word for unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire someone, used as a verb, is to dress them, which is what clothe means.

clue.text: Island choosy passenger underrates showing regular vacancies

indicators.note: each of the three words is emptied of its insides in the same way, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A fussy traveller sniffs at an island holiday because of the empty rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing regular vacancies' empties each word, keeping first and last letters: CY, PR, US.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: They turn article in close cut

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the trimmed word for close
cut tells us to chop the last letter off the word meaning close

parts.note: the close of something is its last part, so last can stand for close
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Instructions for a haircut, where an item is turned into a close crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective describing the cut but is a noun meaning end; 'cut' then trims it and 'in' places the article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathes are machines that rotate a workpiece so it can be shaped: they turn things.

parts.note: a team can be referred to as the men, as in a captain and his men
a tally is a running score or count

explanation.surface: A football side scoring goals with headers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures headed goals; the definition instead means thinking with the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mentally means doing it in the mind, i.e. using one's head.

clue.text: Drill oddly turned top of skull

indicators.note: oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of turned

parts.note: the pan is the top of the skull, as in brainpan

explanation.surface: A grisly bit of surgery: a drill bit turned on the crown of a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes T, R and E from 'turned'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is to bore a hole in the skull with a surgical saw, so it is a kind of drilling.

clue.text: British qualify to receive American support

indicators.note: to receive means the word for qualify takes in the American abbreviation

parts.note: to qualify a statement is to modify or alter it
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A Briton gaining a qualification so as to accept American backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualify' looks like passing an exam but means modify; 'to receive' puts the American abbreviation inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts that hold up a handrail, a physical support.

clue.text: Sunnier seeing willow on leather, finally

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the willow word comes after the letter it sits on
finally asks for the last letter of the word leather

parts.note: an osier is a willow used for basketwork

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: willow bat striking the leather ball makes for a brighter day.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'willow' is the bat and 'leather' the ball; here willow is OSIER and leather gives only its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosier means more hopeful or cheerful, which is a figurative sense of sunnier.

clue.text: Spots son lacking resistance getting weak

indicators.note: lacking says the following letter is missing from the word for spots

parts.note: freckles are small brown spots on the skin
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A spotty boy who cannot fight back is growing feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the R for resistance from FRECKLES, then S for son is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Feckless describes someone lacking vigour or purpose, ineffectual and so weak in character.
